tagline: A county scenic road connects with the approach to Shasta Dam.
intro: Lake Boulevard, County Road A-18, is an officially designated County Scenic Highway within the Whiskeytown-Shasta-Trinity National Recreation Area. Caltrans records its designation in 1981. It connects with Shasta Dam Boulevard, where State Route 151 runs through heavily vegetated country between the dam and the city of Shasta Lake.

The dam changed the surrounding landscape: water storage began in February 1944, and the structure was completed in early 1945. The reservoir flooded traditional Winnemem Wintu lands, including village and burial sites.
At Lake Boulevard’s junction, the separate SR 151 approach continues toward the dam visitor center. Reclamation offers guided tours that cross the dam and enter its powerplant.

moments.title: Lake Boulevard’s scenic section
moments.text: The county scenic designation covers Lake Boulevard, A-18, within the national recreation area. Caltrans granted that recognition in 1981 and states that county scenic highways follow the same program requirements as state routes.

moments.title: Shasta Dam Boulevard junction
moments.text: Summit City developed at the intersection of Shasta Dam and Lake boulevards as one of the communities associated with dam construction. The connecting state highway runs from Shasta Dam to Interstate 5, with the stretch between the dam and Lake Boulevard separately designated scenic.

moments.title: Shasta Dam
moments.text: Shasta Dam impounds the Sacramento River for water storage, flood control, hydroelectricity and protection against saltwater intrusion. The Bureau of Reclamation’s guided tour includes a walk across the top, an elevator descent and a visit to the powerplant. The reservoir also submerged traditional Winnemem Wintu lands and sacred places.
